This strongly suggests cetuximab engaged its intended target EGFR. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The SUVmax decrease from 9.3 to 7.3 (21% reduction) indicates metabolic changes consistent with EGFR pathway modulation and growth inhibition. This suggests the target engagement translated to downstream biological effects. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint (metabolic response) showed a 21% reduction in SUVmax but no statistical significance was reported. However, there was clear evidence of clinical activity with 20% of patients achieving partial response/stable disease and median TTP of 166 days in responders vs 53 days in progressors. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: The trial demonstrates clear subgroup effects - patients achieving disease control had substantially longer TTP (166 days) compared to those with progressive disease (53 days), suggesting the mechanism works in a subset of patients. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a single-arm Phase 2 trial with no control group and relatively small sample size (n=42), making definitive efficacy assessment challenging. The 8-week assessment timeframe appears appropriate for the mechanism.
